newsitem.title: USA: Ill. Supreme Court refuses to speed Tollway appeal.
newsitem.headline: Ill. Supreme Court refuses to speed Tollway appeal.

text.p: Illinois Supreme Court justices have denied the Illinois State Toll Highway Authority's request to accelerate hearing an appeal of a decision overturning its budget practices.
The justices denied the request late last week without comment in the case that has raised credit concerns among the large rating agencies, a Supreme Court clerk said Tuesday.

A Cook County judge in May found that the Toll Authority's practice of budgeting revenues it collects without oversight of the governor or General Assembly failed to meet state constitutional requirements.

Judge Stephen Schiller gave the Toll Authority until Dec 15 to address the oversight issue or be enjoined from all expenditures except those to meet debt service on nearly $1 billion of outstanding debt.

Toll Authority lawyers appealed Schiller's decision under Supreme Court rules calling for the state's highest court to hear direct appeals from the lower courts when a statute has been declared unconstitutional.

Toll Authority officials and a lawyer representing them in the Supreme Court appeal told a General Assembly committee hearing last Wednesday that they expected the high court to overturn Schiller's ruling.
They could not be reached immediately for comment Tuesday on the Supreme Court's decision not to proceed with the case on an expedited basis.
By refusing to hear the case on an accelerated basis, the justices have pushed possible consideration of the case at least until their November term, attorney Lee Schwartz said.
Schwartz and Mike Cherry represent taxpayers who brought the challenge to the Toll Authority practices in 1995.
"They (Supreme Court justices) at least seem willing to give the legislature time to act," Schwartz said.
Moody's Investors Service, Standard & Poor's and Fitch Investors Service all raised credit concerns over the bondholdings.
First National Bank Chicago, a unit of First Chicago NBD Corp, serves as trustee of all Toll Authority outstanding debt and has intervened in the lawsuit on behalf of bondholders.

Schwartz and Cherry have asked to add counts to their ongoing lower court case making Toll Authority commissioners liable for misappropriation of funds. They also seek to put vendors on notice they might not get paid and may be required to return money improperly appropriated to them.
